scope: Reset-only fork support on actual bottle rim, followed by measured-pose geometry checks. No physical delivery/regrasp/placement.

prefix.meaning: Existing selected-scene settling600steps plus accepted bottle9141steps. Prefix replay is neither new manipulation nor independent scene coverage.

support_derivation: Two face-down fork resets put the actual model COM above the measured bottle center. Fork handle points toward the left or right receiver bearing. Reset height comes from the actual hollow-neck collision top plus the inverted fork lower extent and1mm settling clearance. No cap or geometry was added.
result: Both actual reset-only supports are stable and replay exactly. The bounded underneath receiver contact IK gate is unsolved; collision, grasp, delivery and final placement feasibility were not established.

guard_audit.correction: Original support trial guarded fork penetration and bottle displacement but did not separately abort on bottle/table penetration. Every retained frame is now geometrically checked; both participants remain under1mm. Current owned helper/harness add that explicit guard for any future use; no new trial run.

limitations: The two fork resets are explicit support diagnostics, not physically reached intermediate placements.
A stable fork on the bottle does not prove a gripper can deliver it, reach underneath, regrasp or complete the fork setting.
All36receiver searches stop at contact IK with the declared seeds. This does not prove actual palm/camera collision or global physical impossibility.
Intentional support is ordinary contact with the unchanged bottle rim; no attachment, hidden force, model/friction/actuator change or post-start object state write is used.
No new manipulation trial or whole-table success is claimed. Original failures and source snapshots are retained.
promotion: Unpromoted diagnostic dependency; not demonstration eligible.
hash_contract: SHA256 of raw bytes. Tree hashes bind sorted UTF-8 relative POSIX path + NUL + file SHA256 + newline. Raw state/contact maps stay local.
